lessons.0.slides.1.title: Global Burgundy Market Overview
lessons.0.slides.1.content: The Burgundy wine market has experienced explosive growth over the past 20 years. In 2000, DRC's average bottle price was approximately $500–1,000; by 2024 it had exceeded $10,000. The main drivers: (1) the rise of Asian markets (China, Hong Kong, Japan); (2) very limited supply (only 3% of French wine production); (3) quality improvements and international recognition; (4) rising investment demand.
lessons.0.slides.2.title: 💰 DRC Average Price: 25-Year Evolution — From $500 to $15,000
lessons.0.slides.2.content: DRC's average price rose 30-fold from 2000 to 2025, with a compound annual growth rate of 15%. Growth accelerated after the record auction price in 2018. Asian buyers, scarcity, and investment demand are the three main drivers.

lessons.3.slides.1.title: The Psychology of Wine Pricing
lessons.3.slides.1.content: Wine pricing reflects not only cost but also signals quality and confers status. Research shows that for the same wine, the higher the stated price the higher consumers rate it (even in a blind tasting of identical wines). Top Burgundy wines have moved beyond cost-based pricing into the 'Veblen effect' (higher prices generate higher demand). Pricing strategy must consider: competitor pricing, target audience, brand positioning, and scarcity.

lessons.3.slides.2.points.4: Penetration pricing — low price to capture market quickly
lessons.3.slides.2.points.5: Differential pricing — different prices for different channels

lessons.4.slides.2.title: 👥 Burgundy Wine Consumer Segment Types (By Purchase Motivation and Behaviour)
lessons.4.slides.2.content: Enthusiasts (30%) form the core; collectors (15%) contribute the highest ARPU. Social consumers (25%) driven by gifting culture. Accurate segmentation is the foundation of precision marketing.
lessons.4.slides.3.title: The Special Nature of the Asian Market
lessons.4.slides.3.content: Asia (especially mainland China, Hong Kong, and Japan) has become Burgundy's most important market. Key characteristics: (1) strongly brand-oriented (DRC, Leroy, and other prestige names); (2) gifting culture (packaging and brand importance); (3) investment demand (wine as an asset allocation); (4) educational demand (fast learning to catch up); (5) highly digitalised (social media, e-commerce).
lessons.4.slides.4.title: 🌏 Asia's Rising Share of the Burgundy Market: From 5% to 28%
lessons.4.slides.4.content: Asia's market share rose 5-fold from 5% to 28% between 2000 and 2024, making it Burgundy's second-largest market. China, Hong Kong, and Japan are the three main drivers. The rise in DRC prices correlates directly with Asian demand.

lessons.6.slides.1.title: Case Study 1: Berry Bros. & Rudd
lessons.6.slides.1.content: Britain's oldest wine merchant (established 1698) successfully transformed from a traditional retailer into a global luxury wine merchant. Strategy: (1) preserving the experiential value of the physical shop; (2) building a powerful online platform; (3) offering cellar management services; (4) En Primeur futures business; (5) auction and rare-wine sales; (6) educational programmes (WSET partnership). Lesson: combining tradition and innovation, diversifying income streams.
lessons.6.slides.2.title: Case Study 2: The Rise of Vinexpo Asia
lessons.6.slides.2.content: The success of Asia's wine fairs reflects the market's eastward shift. Strategy: (1) targeting high-growth markets; (2) connecting domaines with Asian buyers; (3) equal emphasis on education and commerce; (4) digital exhibition experience; (5) network effects. Lesson: understand market trends and position early in emerging markets.
